articles.title: Marcha Para Jesus em Sorocaba reúne milhares de fiéis na zona leste | G1
articles.standfirst: Concentração de fiéis se reuniu na avenida Dom Aguirre no início da tarde; evento ocorre há 16 anos na cidade.
articles.summary: A Marcha Para Jesus em Sorocaba reuniu os fiéis na avenida Dom Aguirre para uma caminhada até o Parque das Águas, onde foi montado um palco para os shows de música cristã.
articles.body:
A avenida Dom Aguirre foi ocupada por milhares de fiéis que escolheram, no feriado do Dia da Independência, celebrado nesta segunda-feira (7), participar da Marcha Para Jesus, em Sorocaba (SP). O evento é um dos maiores encontros de fé para o público evangélico no Brasil.

O público seguiu a caminhada a pé, acompanhando os trios elétricos com pastores e cantores, até o Parque das Águas. Uma das atrações mais esperada do dia foi a cantora gospel Gabriela Rocha, artista que já soma mais de 10 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais.

Para muitos, a fé foi o combustível para marchar. O trajeto de 1,4 km parece curto, mas é potente para a repercussão de suas orações. Júlia Camargo é uma destas testemunhas, a jovem que trabalha como influenciadora digital destacou o sentimento do dia:

"É a adrenalina que faz a agente acreditar cada vez mais na palavra de Deus", disse.

Jovens marcam presença na Marcha Para Jesus, em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: TV TEM / Reprodução

A concentração teve início a partir das 13h, contando com a participação do público para a caminhada pela cidade.

No Parque das Águas, um palco foi montado para a recepção dos artistas que foram escalados para os shows musicais desta edição. O evento contou com apresentações de artistas de renome da música cristã nacional, como: Gabriela Rocha; Isaias Saad e Renascer Praise.

Shows de música gospel encerram evento da Marcha Para Jesus, em Sorocaba — Foto: TV TEM / Reprodução

A Marcha para Jesus em Sorocaba tem registrado aumento contínuo de participantes nas edições mais recentes. Em 2022, o evento reuniu cerca de 90 mil pessoas. O número subiu para 110 mil em 2023 e alcançou 130 mil em 2024, até atingir o marco de 150 mil fiéis.

Além dos moradores de Sorocaba e municípios da Região Metropolitana, a caminhada atrai caravanas de igrejas vindas de diversos estados brasileiros.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a organização não havia divulgado o balanço oficial da edição de 2026.

Quatro dos oito candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco nas eleições de 2026 tiveram compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (7), em diferentes municípios do estado. As atividades incluem panfletagens, participação em prévia carnavalesca em Olinda, reunião e encontro.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição Raquel Lyra ( PSD ) cumpriu agenda em São Caetano, no Agreste do estado, e em Custódia, no Sertão de Pernambuco. Já o ex-prefeito da capital pernambucana João Campos ( PSB ) esteve no Poço da Panela, na Zona Norte do Recife .

Os candidatos Renan Hallais (Missão), Victor Assis ( PCO ), Guilherme Fonseca ( PSTU ) eProfessor Jeremias do Banco (Democrata) não divulgaram compromissos de campanha.

O ex-vereador do Recife uma compromisso durante o feriado do Dia da Independência. Ele participou do encontro da Troça Carnavalesca Pitombeira dos Quatro Cantos, em Olinda. Na tarde desta segunda-feira (7), a tradicional troça desfilou para abrir o calendário de prévias de carnaval.

Ele prometeu estender o atendimento dos centros estaduais de Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) para jovens e adultos , além de lançar um programa específico de empregabilidade.

A candidata Professora Camila (UP), durante a tarde, fez panfletagem na abertura das prévias do carnaval de Olinda.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição pelo PSD inicidou a agenda participando de uma sabatina ao vivo na TV Tribuna, de 12h. À tarde ela teve reunião com lideranças e empresários em São Caetano, no Agreste do estado. No local, prometeu duplicar a BR-232 da cidade até o município de Serra Talhada , no Sertão.

articles.title: Globo participa de encontro internacional na França para debater o futuro do cinema e da produção audiovisual | G1
articles.standfirst: Em uma declaração conjunta, 120 signatários concordaram com 15 princípios em busca de um ecossistema audiovisual próspero e diversificado.
articles.summary: Em uma declaração conjunta, 120 signatários concordaram com 15 princípios em busca de um ecossistema audiovisual próspero e diversificado.
articles.body:
A cidade de Saint-Paul-de-Vence, na Riviera Francesa, recebeu nesta segunda-feira (7) a Cúpula Lumière. É um encontro internacional dedicado a debater o futuro do cinema e da produção audiovisual. Paulo Marinho representou a Globo , a única empresa brasileira presente no evento. Os presidentes da França e da Coreia do Sul fizeram os discursos de abertura do encontro.

“Há pouco mais de 130 anos, os irmãos Lumière projetaram as primeiras imagens em movimento em uma tela”, lembrou o presidente da França.

Mas o nome da cúpula não foi apenas uma homenagem aos pioneiros do cinema. Lumière significa luz, em francês, e a proposta do encontro foi iluminar o futuro da produção audiovisual em um mundo marcado pela expansão da inteligência artificial e das redes sociais.

“Nunca olhamos para tantas telas. E, ainda assim, de tanto olhar para tudo, corremos o risco de não ver nada”, destacou Emmanuel Macron , presidente da França.

Ele presidiu o evento em Saint-Paul-de-Vence, no sul da França, ao lado de Lee Jae Myung. O presidente da Coreia do Sul ressaltou que as transformações podem virar crise para quem não estiver preparado ou oportunidade para quem souber reagir.

Globo participa de encontro internacional na França para debater o futuro do cinema e da produção audiovisual — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O evento reuniu astros do cinema e representantes dos principais estúdios de Hollywood, da televisão, do streaming, da tecnologia. Em uma declaração conjunta, 120 signatários concordaram com 15 princípios em busca de um ecossistema audiovisual próspero e diversificado. Segundo o documento, esses princípios são baseados em duas convicções: a de que os problemas que afetam a indústria são mais bem combatidos através da cooperação e a de que todas as partes - Estados, empresas, criadores e instituições - têm um papel legítimo e importante a desempenhar nesse esforço conjunto. Entre os 15 princípios, estão:

o investimento em criação e renovação no audiovisual, com novas vozes, histórias, tecnologias e modelos de negócios;

o fortalecimento da cooperação internacional no combate a todas as formas de pirataria;

e o acolhimento da tecnologia, ao mesmo tempo em que a propriedade intelectual é protegida. A criação humana deve permanecer sempre no centro e na fundação das obras.

O apoio a produções mais sustentáveis e a promoção da educação visual como forma de alfabetização para o século XXI também estão entre os 15 princípios da declaração.

A cooperação foi o tema central do painel “Emissoras e plataformas de streaming: antigas rivais, novas estratégias”. Paulo Marinho, diretor-presidente da Globo , participou da discussão sobre parcerias. A Globo foi a única empresa brasileira presente no evento.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra avalanche que matou 11 alpinistas em montanha da Rússia | G1
articles.standfirst: Monte Mizhirgi, onde ocorreu o incidente, fica ao norte da Geórgia, na cordilheira que fica entre o Mar Negro e o Mar Cáspio. Seu pico fica 5.047 metros acima do nível do mar, sendo o sétimo mais alto do Cáucaso.
articles.summary: Monte Mizhirgi, onde ocorreu o incidente, fica ao norte da Geórgia, na cordilheira que fica entre o Mar Negro e o Mar Cáspio.
articles.body:
Pelo menos 11 pessoas morreram e outras seis ficaram feridas após uma avalanche atingir um grupo de alpinistas na região de Cabárdia-Balcária, no Cáucaso do Norte, na Rússia , informaram os serviços de emergência locais.

A avalanche desceu o Monte Mizhirgi — um dos picos mais altos do Cáucaso do Norte russo — por volta das 17h do horário local (11h em Brasília) de domingo (6), atingindo um grupo de 33 alpinistas.

O monte fica ao norte da Geórgia, na cordilheira que fica entre o Mar Negro e o Mar Cáspio. O pico do Mizhirgi fica 5.047 metros acima do nível do mar, sendo o sétimo mais alto do Cáucaso .

Pela contagem mais recente das autoridades, dez alpinistas haviam descido a montanha por conta própria, enquanto o paradeiro de outros seis permanecia desconhecido, segundo os serviços de emergência.

Montanhista registra avalanche no monte Mizhirgi, na Rússia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Mais de 50 equipes de emergência participaram da operação de busca e resgate, mas os trabalhos enfrentam dificuldades pelo terreno de difícil acesso e pelo alto risco de novas avalanches, informaram as autoridades.

Vídeo fagra avalanche no Monte Mizhirgi, na Rússia, em 6 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Ticketless woman held in Bihar with 75 litres of liquor in first AC coach; calm composure stuns cops
articles.summary: Viral video: Neha Jha arrested in Samastipur First AC coach with Ishan Kumar after seizure of 75 litres of foreign liquor; police probe contacts and calls.
articles.body: PATNA: She did not become the subject of a viral video on a stage or through a social-media reel. Instead, 25-year-old Neha Jha drew attention after railway officials opened the door of a locked First AC compartment at Samastipur Junction and allegedly found her with a consignment of foreign liquor. The police interaction that followed was recorded on camera and later circulated widely on social media.What caught viewers’ attention was Neha’s apparent composure during the interaction. Speaking to the officials in fluent English and maintaining a calm demeanour, she appeared unfazed even as the compartment was being searched. The episode, however, has since become a police case involving alleged illegal transportation of liquor.Neha had travelled around 1,100km from New Delhi to Bihar in the H-1 First AC coach with her relative Ishan Kumar. The berth was booked in Ishan’s name, while police alleged that Neha was travelling without a ticket.When the train stopped at Samastipur Junction, RPF and GRP personnel reached the compartment and found the door locked from inside. After repeated knocks, Neha opened the door. The interaction was recorded by the officials. A subsequent search allegedly led to the recovery of around 75 litres of foreign liquor, estimated to be worth about Rs1.5 lakh. Neha and Ishan were arrested and later sent to judicial custody.Neha is from Bari village under Singhia police station area in Darbhanga. She is the youngest of four sisters and is reported to be a graduate of KS College in Darbhanga. She spent part of her education in Darbhanga, where police are now examining her contacts as part of their investigation into the alleged destination of the liquor.Her family background has also come under scrutiny. According to police sources, her father, Sanjay Kumar Jha, was arrested in a liquor-related case nearly two years ago. Her elder sister Nishu Jha was arrested by the excise department on Nov 30, 2025, after she was allegedly found carrying 21 litres of foreign liquor.The family also has two sons. One is still studying in school, while the other reportedly underwent treatment at a de-addiction centre in Muzaffarpur after developing a drug habit following failure in the NEET.Birbal Kumar, SHO of Rail Samastipur and the investigating officer, said, “During initial questioning, Neha reportedly claimed that she was transporting the liquor from Haryana for a wedding that will take place at her home in Dec.” An FIR was filed against Neha and Ishan under Prohibition Act, said the SHO.Police are verifying the claim and investigating whether the stated reason was genuine or was being used to explain the alleged transportation of the liquor.The investigation has now moved beyond the train compartment. Police have seized the mobile phones of Neha and Ishan and are examining their call detail records and WhatsApp conversations. Sources said Neha’s phone contained numbers belonging to several doctors and prominent businessmen in Darbhanga. articles.title: Maharashtra unwraps gifts for Maratha youths on 10th day of Manoj Jarange fast
articles.summary: Maharashtra issues 4 GRs as Jarange’s hunger strike enters day 10, extending OBC-like education benefits, releasing Rs 200 crore, revising SARTHI scholarships, and offering free driving training.
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: With Manoj Jarange’s indefinite hunger strike for Maratha reservation entering its 10th day, Maharashtra govt on Monday announced a series of concessions for Maratha, Kunbi and SEBC youths, even as the quota activist intensified his attack on Mahayuti and called on supporters to gather at Antarvali Sarati on Sept 12.State issued four govt resolutions (GRs) covering education, scholarships, hostel assistance and skill development, apparently seeking to defuse mounting anger within the Maratha community.The decisions include extending educational concessions available to OBC students to Maratha students from the 2026-27 academic year, releasing Rs 200 crore towards pending hostel maintenance allowances, revising SARTHI’s overseas scholarship policy and providing free driving and conductor training to 1,440 Maratha and Kunbi youths.The developments came amid growing concern over Jarange’s health. The activist, who has intermittently accepted saline support during the protest, has reportedly stopped consuming water and is refusing medical treatment.Despite the announcements, Jarange blamed chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy CM Eknath Shinde for delaying reservation benefits for the community and appealed to Marathas to assemble at Antarvali Sarati on Sept 12 to decide the next course of the agitation, including a possible march to Mumbai.Under one of the GRs, all educational benefits currently available to OBC students will be extended to Maratha students through the Directorate of Technical Education and universities from the next academic year.The higher and technical education department has also released Rs 200 crore for pending Dr Punjabrao Deshmukh hostel maintenance allowances for EBC, EWS and SEBC students. The funds have been made available through supplementary demands approved during the monsoon session.In another significant decision, govt revised the SARTHI overseas scholarship scheme. Tuition fees will now be paid directly to foreign universities; the earlier funding ceiling has been removed. Students will also receive an additional annual maintenance/contingency allowance of $1,500, or £1,100. A new merit-listing mechanism based on QS rankings has also been introduced. A fresh merit-listing system based on QS rankings has also been introduced.SARTHI has additionally tied up with the Institute of Driving Training and Research, Pimpri-Chinchwad, to provide free LMV, HMV and conductor training to 1,440 Maratha and Kunbi youths from Oct 1, with a target of ensuring employment or self-employment for at least 1,000 beneficiaries.Meanwhile, revenue minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil reviewed the process of displaying Kunbi records traced from historical documents, including the Hyderabad Gazetteer, at the village level. In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district, the records have been uploaded on the district administration’s website and can be accessed through mobile phones. Gram panchayats have also been instructed to display records pertaining to their respective villages.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: DU’s hostel crunch is more than a decade-old problem. Can Delhi learn from universities abroad?
articles.summary: Delhi University’s decade-old hostel shortage persists: ~7,000 seats for 71,600 new UG students, boosting pricey PG demand; abroad, universities aid off-campus housing.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For thousands of students coming to Delhi University from outside the city, securing admission does not necessarily mean securing a place to stay.Only a handful of colleges have hostels and admission into them is harder than getting into university to begin with.The gap has fuelled a thriving private PG economy around college clusters. The shortage is not new. In a written reply to a Rajya Sabha question in Nov 2016, Union human resource development ministry, citing DU, said the university had 19 hostels with a combined capacity of 3,580 students.Including accommodation provided by some colleges, estimates put hostel availability at 6,000 seats, while DU admitted at least 60,000 students annually.A decade later, the gap remains substantial. In 2026, DU has 91 colleges, with 69 colleges and departments participating in undergraduate admissions. Around 71,600 new UG students were admitted in 2026-27, while about half of DU students are from outside Delhi, as per college estimates. Against this, there are around 7,000 hostel seats. The university has 20 main hostels across its North and South campuses, while 20 colleges have hostel facilities and 71 do not, according to officials.The numbers become starker against DU’s overall student population. Its 2024-25 annual report, the latest available on its website, records 2.1 lakh undergraduate students and 34,520 postgraduate students, including PhD scholars -- nearly 2.5 lakh in all.Miranda House, for example, has an overall student strength of 5,375, but its hostel accomodates only about 370 students. For 2026-27, the college has offered just 90 hostel seats to first-year students. Sri Venkateswara College, with an overall student strength of around 4,600, has hostel capacity for 150 students, with just 50 seats available to first-year students.Residence has, in fact, figured in DU’s governing framework since its early years. Section 33 of Delhi University Act, 1922, says every student, other than one studying through correspondence, “shall reside in a college or a hall, or under such conditions as may be prescribed by the ordinances”. A university official, however, said the provision “in today’s times should not be read as a guarantee of a university hostel room to every student”.For students arriving from another state, an admission confirmation can therefore mark the beginning of another search for somewhere to live. Limited hostel seats leave many turning to PGs, private hostels and rented flats in areas such as Vijay Nagar and Malka Ganj, near North Campus, and Satya Niketan, near South Campus.Students say the private market can mean paying more for cramped and poorly maintained accommodation. “There should be more hostels for students. Outside, everything is expensive and not maintained. I don’t know where students are supposed to go,” a DU student said.Reliance on private housing is not unique to Delhi. What differs in some university systems abroad is the support provided to students navigating the private rental market.Indroneil B Biswas, who studied in Oregon in the US, recalled that a department administrator contacted him even before his arrival about applying for campus accommodation with another international student. “The admins helped us navigate on-campus housing,” he said, though accommodation was not automatic. Universities there also provide off-campus housing listings, information on tenants’ rights and, in some cases, access to student legal services for housing disputes.In Manchester in the UK, Manchester Student Homes, a university-run service, helps students navigate private accommodation through listings and an accreditation scheme requiring participating landlords and agents to follow a Code of Standards. It also offers housing advice and assistance with disputes. articles.title: Studies can wait, classrooms at DU turn shelters for displaced students
articles.summary: Delhi University colleges turned classrooms into temporary shelters after the Satya Niketan PG building collapse, halting classes and providing food, counselling and helplines.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Classrooms and other facilities in several Delhi University colleges were turned into temporary shelters Monday as institutions suspended classes and opened their campuses to students displaced after the PG building collapse in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan.Colleges put up mattresses in health centres, staff and guest rooms to accommodate students and arranged for food and counselling for those in distress. Several PGs in the area also shut their doors and asked residents to vacate, while some were reportedly sealed amid concerns over the condition of the buildings.DU has directed colleges to check their admission rolls, identify students living in the affected area and reach out to them to shift to the campus for their safety. Venkateswara College, Motilal Nehru College, Jesus and Mary College, Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, Maitreyi College, Ram Lal Anand College, Bhagat Singh College and Aryabhatta College, among others, have issued these notices offering shelter and food support to the students.A WhatsApp group of college principals and South Campus director Rajni Abbi has also been set up to share updates and coordinate assistance. The university has offered the AICTE guest house to parents who need accommodation while visiting Delhi, officials said.Female students have been allowed to take shelter in any college, while male students are being accommodated at their respective colleges after ID verification. Colleges have issued helpline numbers for students seeking food and shelter. NCC teams from several colleges also appealed for donations of water, food and bedsheets and distributed supplies at the site.At the collapse site, student volunteers from nearby colleges searched for classmates believed to have been living in the collapsed building. “Our college WhatsApp group shared six profiles of senior students from our college. We have come looking for them,” said Harshika, a first-year Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College student.Students living in adjoining buildings were also forced to leave. Ananya, an Odisha student staying in the building next to the one that collapsed, said her building had tilted and was subsequently vacated. “There was a sudden huge noise. I opened the window and saw a huge cloud of dust. I immediately realised the building had collapsed, so I ran for my life and came out,” she said. Her parents have since asked her to return home.At Venkateswara, a student who narrowly escaped the collapse broke down and was taken to a counsellor. The college principal Vajala Ravi said he slept with displaced students brought to the campus. “These are old buildings that have become dangerous.... We are doing all we can to help the students,” he said.Motilal Nehru College principal (morning) Yogeshwar Sharma said the college staff were present at the hospital trying to trace students whose phones were unreachable and were contacting their parents. Three students reported to be dead are believed to be from the college, he said.According to officials, 72 students — 46 boys and 26 girls — stayed at Venkateswara overnight, while around 50 stayed at Motilal Nehru College. Ram Lal Anand College arranged for 50 students, though they later left after having food. Many others moved to friends’ or relatives’ homes by Monday morning.Meanwhile, protests continued. ABVP held a late-night protest Sunday and stormed the MCD office, demanding the commissioner’s resignation. Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP) began a sit-in at Satya Niketan, demanding that DU pay rent for students forced to live outside campus due to the hostel shortage, while NSUI, ABVP, SFI and AISA protested near the site, demanding action. articles.title: Don’t hurt Sanatani traditions, CM Suvendu tells Puja organisers
articles.summary: CM Suvendu Adhikari announces Bengal Durga Puja rules: no immersion carnival, DJ ban, Ashtami liquor closure, Rs 1 lakh grant, free power, 3-day immersion limit.
articles.body: By: Soumitra NandiKOLKATA: All Durga Puja pandals and themes should keep in mind and conform to the festival’s original significance and tradition, CM Suvendu Adhikari told organisers during a meeting on Monday while announcing several breaks from the celebration that Kolkata and Bengal had got used to seeing in the last few years.The state administration would not organise any immersion carnival but there would be roadshows during the festival days, besides the Mahalaya programme at Eden Gardens the state announced a few days ago, he said.A partial ban on the sale of alcohol would also be re-entering the Durga Puja calendar this year, with Adhikari announcing liquor vends would be shut on Ashtami.The CM announced a Durga Puja grant of Rs 1 lakh for organisers but appealed to big-budget pujas not to apply for it. The state administration last year gave a grant of Rs 1.1 lakh each to all 45,000-odd registered clubs and puja committees.Adhikari also asked private electricity provider CESC and state-owned WBSEDCL to provide free electricity to Durga Puja organisers; the waiver was 80% last year. CESC managing director Vineet Sikka later said the company would comply with the CM’s directive.Theme-based pujas would be allowed, the CM said, but committees must ensure their themes did not hurt or undermine Sanatani traditions and Bengal’s heritage and culture. There would be a complete ban on DJ music during puja days as well as immersion, he added, urging organisers not to block National Highways.The immersion carnival that Kolkata hosted till last year was imposed upon puja committees, Adhikari said, while unveiling the state’s this year’s plan to host a grand four-hour Mahalaya programme at Eden Gardens that would be organised jointly by the tourism and information & cultural affairs departments. “It will feature drone and fireworks as we welcome the Goddess’s arrival. We have invited PM Narendra Modi to the event,” he added.The state tourism department would also organise a puja programme in Digha and six cities across Bengal would host two-day events after Mahalaya, Adhikari said, adding that four ghats in Kolkata would be dressed up for the festival.All idols will have to be immersed within three days of Dashami. “Idol immersion is done according to the almanac. It cannot happen according to one’s whims. We need a cut-off date,” he explained.“I had earlier said committees with small budgets would be given assistance. But I do not want to misuse the CM’s powers and so will leave it to puja committees. But I appeal to committees that can host the puja without financial assistance not to apply (for it). Those who really need the grant should apply,” Adhikari said, adding that the previous regime had increased the grant from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1.1 lakh over the years but it had not yielded political dividends and, instead, made many committees dependent on the assistance.The administration would make special arrangements to facilitate puja visits for persons with disabilities and residents of old-age homes, Adhikari said, clarifying that the state would continue to award puja committees with prizes in categories like best idol, best pandal, best eco-friendly puja, best crowd management, best public turnout and best idol-maker/artist. Only experts with knowledge about Durga Puja will be judges.Police and fire brigade personnel, state health and transport departments employees as well as those of urban local bodies who would be on duty during puja would get two days’ paid holiday after the festival, Adhikari said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Forget the Mediterranean diet, I'm eating nothing but food from Shetland for a month
articles.summary: Dr Alex Armitage is eating only food grown, reared or caught in Shetland during September.
articles.body:
Could you survive a month eating only food produced in your local area?

It would be difficult enough to do in a city, town or village on the mainland. Dr Alex Armitage is doing it in Shetland.

As part of Shetland Food Month, the consultant paediatrician has set himself the challenge of surviving on just local produce for the month of September.

He's already been out in his kayak to catch fish, he's been foraging for mushrooms and berries, and he's enjoyed vegetables from his neighbour's croft.

Armitage, who is also a councillor with the Scottish Greens, said he grew up in London where he heard stories of his granny's childhood in Shetland.

He was fascinated by how people could survive on the archipelago, more than 100 miles north of the Scottish mainland.

Now the population relies on the regular deliveries of food transported by Northlink ferry from Aberdeen

But Armitage is concerned that increasingly stormy seas could leave the islands cut off for extended periods - and the supermarket shelves empty.

"If we had a week the ferry doesn't come to Shetland and Tesco runs out of food, what would happen if that happened for longer and we really had to survive by ourselves here," he said.

"It got me thinking could people actually survive on Shetland produce? I thought I would live out that thought experiment."

The father-of-one said he liked to start the day with a big breakfast - egg, fish and vegetables "fired up" in Shetland butter.

"This morning I made Eggs Florentine with some eggs people have donated," he added.

"I've also got a big shipment of herring which is a wonderful and a very traditional Shetland fish to fry."

Most of the produce has been donated to him, but he buys Shetland milk and cream from a local shop.

He added: "I like to use the opportunity of the Shetland Food Month to look deeper behind some of the stories about our food in Shetland.

"I've been out foraging. I've got mushrooms from Burra. I've just picked up blackberries from one of the lanes in Lerwick and I've been out fishing as well - I have a kayak.

"Shetland tatties are very plentiful and very available. Shetland tatties are my favourite source of carbohydrate without a shadow of a doubt. Getting other sources of carbohydrates is extremely difficult."

But of course there are some items that just can't be produced in the cool Shetland climate.

Asked what he is missing the most during his month-long challenge, he said: "It's got to be caffeine."

"Fortunately I've got over the caffeine withdrawals," he said.

"They were really hard, about three days. It's not pleasant, you just have a constant headache all the time."

This is the third year that Armitage has challenged himself to eat just Shetland produce for a month.

He said it was a fun activity but it was also an important reminder of the fragility of food security in the islands.

articles.title: A 72-year-old man inherited nearly 900 acres from his uncles; after decades restoring the forest, he gave the land to a Native American tribe
articles.summary: US News: Gary Verbrugge, a 72-year-old man in Washington state, inherited nearly 900 acres of woodland linked to his family for almost a century. Rather than t.
articles.body: Gary Verbrugge, a 72-year-old man in Washington state, inherited nearly 900 acres of woodland linked to his family for almost a century. Rather than treating the property as an asset to be sold or developed, he spent decades helping restore its forests, waterways and wildlife habitats. His work eventually led to a decision that would shape the land’s future long after him: the transfer of this 885 acres to the ‘Kalispel Tribe of Indians.’ The property, which lies along the Little Spokane River, is home to a remarkable mix of forests, wetlands and open areas used by animals including moose, elk, wolves, bears and cougars. As reported by the Inland Northwest Land Conservancy, the donation brings together private conservation and Indigenous stewardship, giving the Tribe long-term responsibility for a landscape with deep cultural and ecological importance for generations to come.72-year-old man restore nearly 900 acres before giving it to a Native American tribeThe story of the property began long before Gary Verbrugge became responsible for it. According to the Inland Northwest Land Conservancy, his father’s uncles, ‘Will and Harry Storms,’ bought adjoining pieces of land in 1927. When they died, the properties passed to the Verbrugge family. The nearly 900-acre landscape sits along the Little Spokane River north of Spokane and contains several distinct environments. River bottoms, marshes, steep forests and high ridges exist within the same property, creating a varied habitat for wildlife.But the forest did not remain untouched over the decades. Industrial logging affected the land, and Verbrugge later worked to improve its condition. Often assisted by volunteers, he replanted trees by hand, restored vegetation along streams, stabilised riverbanks and helped create more shade and better habitat. Those efforts were not about making the property look greener. They reflected a long-term commitment to allowing the land and the animals that depended on it to recover. The Inland Northwest Land Conservancy reported that the woodland is used by moose, elk, deer, cougars, bobcats, goshawks, bears and wolves.Why did the Kalispel Tribe become the future steward of the landThe Inland Northwest Land Conservancy reported that the Kalispel Tribe was developing its first Tribally owned and managed community forest, with a focus on natural resource education. Its goals closely matched Verbrugge's own hopes for his woodland. Conversations followed about the possibility of the Tribe becoming the long-term owner and steward of the property. Verbrugge said he believed the Tribe would take good care of the land and its wildlife. He was particularly impressed by the detailed forest planning carried out by specialists working with the Tribe.Ray Entz, director of Wildlife and Terrestrial Resources for the Kalispel Natural Resources Department, said Verbrugge's decision was driven by a deep affection for wildlife. He also explained that the tribe was a suitable long-term steward because of its permanent connection to the land. That connection carries particular significance because the Kalispel Tribe's reservation is relatively small compared with its much wider ancestral landscape. According to the Conservancy, that ancestral region extends across parts of north-east Washington, northern Idaho, western Montana and Canada. Owning more land can provide opportunities for Tribal members to hunt, fish, gather and take part in other cultural activities that depend on healthy, functioning landscapes.A conservation commitment by Gary built over many yearsVerbrugge began securing the land's future before deciding to donate it to the Kalispel Tribe. In 2007, he worked with the Inland Northwest Land Conservancy to place a permanent conservation easement on 605 acres. The agreement meant that the property could not later be subdivided or developed. It was an important step, but the conservation area eventually became even larger. According to the Conservancy, Verbrugge later bought an adjoining 280 acres and added that land to the conservation easement as well. The expanded project was completed in late 2025. Verbrugge had to consider who would care for it over the long term. The answer emerged through a growing relationship with the Kalispel Tribe of Indians.Restoring the forest also meant preparing it for a challenging futureThe handover was not the end of work on the property. The Tribe's natural resources team spent several years working with Verbrugge on forest management. According to the Conservancy, the team helped develop a formal plan, secure state funding and guide work including thinning and reducing fuels across roughly 40 acres. The aim was to improve habitat while reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire. The property's mix of forests and wet areas could also make the landscape more resilient as conditions change. Protecting the forest meant looking ahead instead of preserving it exactly as it was.The benefits may also reach beyond the boundaries of Verbrugge's former property. The Conservancy reported that the surrounding forested landscape contributes cold, clean water to the Little Spokane River. Protected land elsewhere along the river system adds to a wider network of connected habitats and waterways.A gift that placed the future of the land beyond one lifetimeAccording to ‘ImpactfulNinja,’ the donation is an example of how private landowners can make lasting contributions to conservation while supporting Indigenous stewardship. For Verbrugge, however, the decision was rooted in a far more personal relationship with the place. He had inherited land shaped by generations before him, watched it change and spent years helping restore it. Instead of leaving its future to chance, he chose a steward whose connection to the wider landscape stretches far beyond a single lifetime. The Inland Northwest Land Conservancy said the Kalispel Tribe has committed to caring for the land in ways that benefit nature, culture and the community.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Thousands across Germany protest against AfD after election victory
articles.summary: Thousands of people across Germany protested against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) on Monday following its landslide victory in the state elect...
articles.body:
Thousands of people across Germany protested against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) following its victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election.

The protests, organized by Campact and Fridays for Future, saw participants in Berlin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Essen, Potsdam, Hesse, and Kassel calling for action against the AfD.

The AfD won the election but did not secure an absolute majority, prompting concerns about the possibility of Germany's first AfD-led state government.

Thousands of people across Germany protested against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) on Monday following its landslide victory in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt.

In Berlin, police estimated a crowd of around 5,000 had gathered at Brandenburg Gate and said the demonstration passed without incident. Organizers put the number of participants at around 14,000.

The rally was called at short notice by campaign organization Campact and the Fridays for Future climate movement.

Among those taking part were prominent German climate activist Luisa Neubauer and the lead candidates of the Greens and The Left in Berlin's state election on September 20.

Protesters carried banners with slogans including "Fascism is not an alternative" and "Stop AfD Nazis! End racism and social cuts," while crowds chanted: "All together against fascism!"

The party won Sunday's election by a wide margin but fell short of an absolute majority, leaving open the possibility of Germany's first AfD-led state government.

The domestic intelligence agency has classified the AfD's state branch as "confirmed right-wing extremist."

Protests were also called in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, where a new state parliament will be elected later this month and the AfD is leading in the polls.

In Schwerin, according to police reports, several hundred demonstrators gathered, while in Rostock, more than 500 people came together for a communal sing-along.

In Essen, about 1,200 people gathered, according to police. Carrying rainbow flags and cardboard signs with messages such as "Ban the AfD now" and "No place for Nazis," the participants marched through the city centre.

Hundreds of people also gathered in Potsdam to protest against the AfD, as did others in Hesse. Around 80 people protested in Kassel.

Police said about 2,500 people demonstrated in Frankfurt on Sunday, calling for a review of the possibility of banning the AfD.

articles.title: Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of killing seven in Yemen prison air strike
articles.summary: Houthi-run media outlet released footage of destruction after alleged Saudi air strike on al-Hazm prison.
articles.body:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels have accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out an air strike on a prison in the northern city of al-Hazm, killing seven people, including a child.

The strike on the Central Corrective Facility in al-Jawf province, on the Yemeni side of the border with Saudi Arabia, also wounded at least seven people, including a woman, Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, said on Monday.

The Houthi-run Al Masirah TV channel aired footage it said showed the aftermath of the alleged attack, including a collapsed building and people searching through the rubble.

Saudi Arabia has not commented on the allegations.

Al Masirah TV also released footage it claims shows Houthi forces using ballistic missiles to attack Saudi supply trucks containing military equipment at a border crossing in Yemen’s Hadramout province.

Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of “committing massacres” in al-Jawf, flying reconnaissance drones and supplying mercenaries with weaponry.

“The ongoing Saudi aggression against Yemen will not go unpunished, and the Saudi enemy must bear the consequences of its crimes against the Yemeni people,” he said.

Saree also claimed that the Houthis had shot down four Saudi reconnaissance drones over the previous 24 hours, including a CH-4 drone that he said was carrying out “hostile missions” in al-Jawf.

“This aircraft is the second of this type that was shot down during the past 12 hours, and the fourth during the past 24 hours,” he added.

Dually, Riyadh has not commented on Saree’s allegations.

The Houthi claims come as fighting between the group and Yemen’s internationally recognised government has flared up in recent weeks. The Yemeni government said it made significant territorial gains against the Houthis, including in the al-Jawf, Bayda, Dahle, and Marib provinces on Sunday.

Over the past days, government-aligned forces conducted counterattacks in Taiz and Hodeidah after the Houthis launched a major offensive in a struggle to control the critical Bab al-Mandeb strait, with hundreds of people reportedly killed over the past 24 hours.

UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg called Monday on the country’s warring parties to halt hostilities and exercise maximum restraint, warning that the latest escalation could spiral into a full-scale war.

Air strikes on prisons have occurred several times during Yemen’s decade-long war. In 2022, the Saudi-led coalition struck a detention facility in Saada province, killing at least 87 prisoners and wounding about 266 others.

In 2019, the coalition struck a Houthi-run detention facility in Dhamar province, killing more than 100 people and wounding dozens.

articles.title: Morre cão que caiu em galeria de macrodrenagem em Balneário Camboriú | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal chegou a ser retirado com vida da galeria, mas não resistiu. Prefeitura lamentou morte e reforçou importância de respeitar barreiras de segurança da obra.
articles.summary: Animal chegou a ser retirado com vida da galeria, mas não resistiu.
articles.body:
O cachorro que precisou ser resgatado pelos bombeiros após cair na galeria de macrodrenagem morreu na segunda-feira (7), informou a Prefeitura de Balneário Camboriú , cidade do Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina onde ocorreu o acidente. A queda foi no domingo (6).

O cão, chamado de Jean Pierre, caiu em uma abertura na Praia Central. Em nota, o município lamentou a morte e reforçou importância de respeitar barreiras de segurança da obra ( leia a nota na íntegra no final da reportagem ).

Guarda-vidas entraram dentro da galeria para fazer resgate

A galeria onde o cachorro caiu é de difícil acesso e com presença de água. A abertura na areia tem cerca de 1 metro quadrado.

Para o resgate, dois guarda-vidas entraram dentro da galeria. Foi constatado que a profundidade era de cerca de 1,70 metro e a água fazia uma leve correnteza.

Os guarda-vidas acompanharam o sentido da correnteza e, após 10 minutos de buscas, acharam o cão, que estava a cerca de 60 metros da abertura da galeria onde ele havia caído.

Com uma escada, os guarda-vidas saíram da estrutura, trazendo o cachorro. O animal estava muito cansado e não conseguiu ficar em pé .

Cão é resgatado após cair dentro de galeria de macrodrenagem na Praia Central de Balneário Camboriú — Foto: Reprodução/CBMSC

O cachorro foi secado com panos, para ser aquecido, e o quadro de saúde dele melhorou. Depois, foi entregue à tutora, que se comprometeu a levá-lo em um veterinário.

O município disse que, apesar de o local estar cercado, o cachorro conseguiu ultrapassar as barreiras e acabou caindo.

A prefeitura destacou ainda que a importância de respeitar as barreiras de segurança das obras. "Essas estruturas não devem ser rompidas, removidas ou danificadas. A violação ou depredação das barreiras, além de colocar pessoas e animais em risco".

Prefeitura afirma que abertura da galeria estava sinalizada e cercada ainda antes de cão cair — Foto: PMBC/Divulgação

Confira abaixo a íntegra da nota da Prefeitura de Balneário Camboriú sobre a morte do cão.

A Prefeitura de Balneário Camboriú lamenta, com pesar, a morte do cão Jean Pierre, confirmada nesta segunda-feira (7). O animal não resistiu após cair, neste domingo (6), em uma abertura da galeria de macrodrenagem na faixa de areia da Praia Central.

Logo após o ocorrido, a Secretaria de Planejamento e Desenvolvimento Urbano entrou em contato com a empresa responsável pela execução da obra, que já tomou as providências necessárias para reforçar a segurança das áreas que ainda permanecem em intervenção.

Além disso, conforme já informado neste domingo, a empresa já havia sido formalmente comunicada para concluir os serviços remanescentes, e, após descumprimentos de prazos, a Administração Pública adotou medidas administrativas cabíveis para a penalização da empresa.

O município presta solidariedade à família enlutada e reforça a importância de respeitar as barreiras de segurança da obra, que têm a função de impedir o acesso às áreas de intervenção e proteger a população. articles.title: EUA afundam embarcação no Pacífico e atribuem barco a facção equatoriana | G1
articles.standfirst: Militares americanos dizem que barco equatoriano servia como base flutuante de abastecimento para operações de tráfico; é a quinta embarcação afundada em menos de duas semanas.
articles.summary: Militares americanos dizem que barco equatoriano servia como base flutuante de abastecimento para operações de tráfico; é a quinta embarcação afundada em menos de duas semanas.
articles.body:
O Comando Sul dos Estados Unidos afundou nesta segunda-feira (7) mais uma embarcação equatoriana que, segundo as autoridades americanas, estaria ligada ao grupo criminoso Los Choneros. Veja no vídeo acima.

A ação é a mais recente ofensiva dos EUA contra barcos e embarcações na América Latina supostamente envolvidos com o tráfico de drogas.

Segundo comunicado do Comando Sul, uma força-tarefa conjunta interceptou uma embarcação usada como posto flutuante de abastecimento que dava suporte a operações ilícitas de narcotráfico no leste do Oceano Pacífico.

Os ocupantes foram retirados da embarcação e serão transferidos às autoridades equatorianas.

Familiares de tripulantes do barco María Candelaria aguardam notícias em Manta, no Equador, após a embarcação ser interceptada por autoridades dos EUA sob suspeita de ligação com o tráfico de drogas. — Foto: Ariel Ochoa / Associated Press

Vídeo divulgado pelos militares mostra agentes embarcando no navio, um helicóptero sobrevoando a área e, por fim, um projétil atingindo e afundando a embarcação.

O comunicado afirma ainda que as forças americanas seguem realizando “operações precisas e profissionais para desmantelar as redes logísticas que alimentam o tráfico de drogas no Hemisfério Ocidental”.

As autoridades do Equador não comentaram o caso de imediato. A embarcação afundada, cujo nome não foi divulgado, é a quinta alvo das forças americanas em menos de duas semanas.

Na semana passada, o barco pesqueiro María Candelaria foi atingido no Pacífico, de acordo com informações do Comando Sul, em operação coordenada com autoridades equatorianas.

A Marinha do Equador localizou 26 tripulantes da embarcação, que chegaram no domingo ao porto de Manta. Outros oito pescadores do barco Conquista II também foram encontrados, enquanto familiares cobravam informações sobre seu paradeiro.

Outras duas embarcações, OM2 e Los Tres Hermanos, também foram afundadas, segundo relatos de seus tripulantes. Recentemente, o Comando Sul as identificou na rede social X como “postos flutuantes de abastecimento para múltiplas embarcações envolvidas em operações ilícitas de tráfico de drogas”.

Os Estados Unidos afirmam que todos os barcos tinham ligação com o grupo Los Choneros, classificado por Washington como organização terrorista estrangeira.

Esses casos se somam aos de outras três embarcações cujas tripulações equatorianas afirmam ter sido interceptadas por forças americanas neste ano. No caso do barco Fiorella, oito pescadores continuam desaparecidos desde janeiro. As tripulações das outras embarcações retornaram ao Equador após serem levadas para El Salvador.

Pelo menos 227 pessoas morreram em 68 ataques realizados pelo governo dos EUA contra embarcações no Caribe e no Pacífico desde o início dessas operações, há mais de um ano. Críticos questionam tanto a legalidade quanto a eficácia das ações.

EUA interceptam quinta embarcação em menos de duas semanas no Pacífico. — Foto: Reprodução / Comando Sul dos EUA

Em pelo menos um caso, autoridades equatorianas afirmaram não ter encontrado provas de que um sobrevivente de um dos ataques tivesse participado de qualquer atividade criminosa.

O governo Trump busca ampliar acordos com países aliados para estender sua ofensiva ao território de nações latino-americanas. Neste mês, durante visita ao Panamá, o secretário de Defesa dos EUA, Pete Hegseth, afirmou que Colômbia, Guatemala e Honduras concordaram em permitir operações militares conjuntas contra grupos criminosos em seus territórios. A Guatemala negou ter firmado tal acordo. O Equador iniciou missões semelhantes com os Estados Unidos em março.

articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.055 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 70 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta terça-feira (8), em São Paulo.

No concurso do último domingo (6), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Comunidades rurais de Montes Claros recebem melhorias na infraestrutura | G1
articles.standfirst: Os serviços incluem recuperação de estradas, pontes e mata-burros, além de serviços de limpeza e pintura.
articles.summary: Os serviços incluem recuperação de estradas, pontes e mata-burros, além de serviços de limpeza e pintura.
articles.body:
O Município de Montes Claros, através da Secretaria de Agricultura, Pecuária e Desenvolvimento Rural, tem intensificado os investimentos no campo, promovendo melhorias na infraestrutura das comunidades, fortalecendo o apoio aos produtores e ampliando os serviços públicos oferecidos à população rural. As ações integram um planejamento permanente que busca garantir melhores condições de trafegabilidade nas estradas vicinais e ampliar a qualidade de vida das famílias que vivem na área rural.

Com uma das maiores extensões de estradas rurais de Minas Gerais, Montes Claros possui mais de 5 mil quilômetros de vias vicinais, fundamentais para o escoamento da produção agrícola, o transporte escolar, o acesso aos serviços de saúde e a mobilidade das comunidades. Nos últimos dias o Município intensificou o programa Giro no Campo, recuperando estradas rurais, executando serviços de patrolamento, cascalhamento, drenagem, construção e manutenção de mata-burros, além da recuperação de pontes e bueiros em diversas regiões.

Geraldo Eleutério, morador de Estreito de Miralta: “possibilidade de comercializar o que é produzido aqui” — Foto: Rogeriano Cardoso

Depois de muito tempo de espera, a comunidade de Estreito de Miralta está recebendo os serviços de patrolamento e cascalhamento das estradas, garantindo melhores condições de tráfego. Geraldo Eleutério, morador da comunidade, destacou o trabalho que está sendo feito: “essa obra vai prover a comunidade da possibilidade de comercializar o que é produzido aqui”.

As estradas das comunidades de Olhos D'Água e Nova Esperança também estão sendo beneficiadas. Com estradas de qualidade, quem vive e produz no campo ganha mais agilidade para transportar sua produção, facilitando a comercialização e fortalecendo a economia rural. É mais dignidade para o produtor, mais desenvolvimento para a zona rural e mais qualidade de vida para quem depende dessas estradas todos os dias.

São Pedro da Garça recebe pintura para voar mais alto — Foto: Rogeriano Cardoso

Além das obras de infraestrutura, o Município tem realizado o Mutirão de Serviços na zona rural. No último final de semana o mutirão foi realizado em São Pedro da Garça, levando cuidado para a comunidade. Foram realizados os serviços de capina, tapa-buracos, limpeza geral das ruas, pintura de meio-fio e revitalização da pintura dos pisos e escadas da praça, deixando os espaços públicos mais seguros, bonitos e acolhedores para toda a população.

articles.title: Ainda pode nevar no RS? Veja previsão do tempo nesta terça-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Atuação de massa de ar frio associada a um sistema de alta pressão mantém o céu com poucas nuvens e sem previsão de chuva, enquanto as temperaturas continuam baixas no início do dia.
articles.summary: Atuação de massa de ar frio associada a sistema de alta pressão mantém o céu com poucas nuvens e sem previsão de chuva, enquanto as temperaturas continuam baixas no início do dia.
articles.body:
Após a neve registrada na Serra do RS no domingo (6) , o Rio Grande do Sul segue sob influência do frio nesta terça-feira (8) . O amanhecer será gelado em todo o estado, com possibilidade de geada , mas a previsão é de tempo firme e sol entre poucas nuvens.

❄️ De acordo com a Climatempo Meteorologia, geada e neve não são a mesma coisa. Enquanto a geada surge sobre superfícies resfriadas próximas ao solo, a partir da umidade presente no ar, a neve se desenvolve no interior das nuvens, onde cristais de gelo se formam e precipitam até o chão.

Nesta terça-feira, a atuação de uma massa de ar frio ainda associada a um sistema de alta pressão mantém o céu com poucas nuvens e sem previsão de chuva, enquanto as temperaturas continuam baixas no início do dia.

Há possibilidade de geada no Sudoeste do RS durante o amanhecer. As menores temperaturas previstas são de cerca de 3°C em Santiago, Ijuí e Quaraí. Em Cruz Alta e Santo Ângelo, os termômetros devem marcar em torno de 4°C nas primeiras horas do dia.

Apesar do frio nas primeiras horas da manhã, os termômetros devem subir gradualmente ao longo da tarde . Em algumas cidades, as máximas chegam a 23°C, como em São Luiz Gonzaga, Santa Rosa e Horizontina.

Na capital, o sol aparece entre poucas nuvens ao longo da terça. A mínima prevista é de aproximadamente 10°C, enquanto a máxima pode alcançar 22°C.

A previsão indica alteração nas condições meteorológicas a partir de quarta-feira (9) . Um cavado em médios níveis da atmosfera, associado a um sistema de baixa pressão entre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai, favorece o retorno da chuva em parte do estado .

Mesmo assim, a maior parte do Rio Grande do Sul deve continuar com tempo firme . As precipitações tendem a ocorrer de forma isolada, com intensidade entre fraca e moderada e, em pontos específicos, mais forte. A tendência é que os volumes se concentrem principalmente no noroeste gaúcho.

Na quinta-feira (10) , as instabilidades seguem influenciando parte da Região Sul do país. No Rio Grande do Sul, a Faixa Norte continua com condições para pancadas de chuva de moderada a forte intensidade , acompanhadas de trovoadas e possibilidade de temporais isolados .

Nas demais regiões, a expectativa é de predomínio de tempo mais estável , embora não se descarte ocorrência isolada de chuva em alguns pontos. O ar mais seco mantém as manhãs amenas, com elevação gradual da temperatura durante a tarde.

Até o fim de 2026, o calendário ainda reserva cinco feriados nacionais. Desses, quatro podem ser emendados com o fim de semana, criando oportunidades para períodos prolongados de descanso (veja o calendário abaixo) .

Mesmo nos feriados nacionais, porém, nem todos os trabalhadores têm folga. A legislação permite o funcionamento de serviços essenciais e de outras atividades autorizadas a operar nessas datas.

⚠️ Nesses casos, quem trabalhar no feriado pode ter direito a remuneração em dobro ou folga compensatória , conforme as regras aplicáveis.

articles.title: HasanAbi makes explosive Lindsay Clancy trial claim, says medical system “failed” her
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, widely known as HasanAbi, has entered the conversation surrounding the Lindsay Clancy trial, arguing that the case cannot.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, widely known as HasanAbi, has entered the conversation surrounding the Lindsay Clancy trial, arguing that the case cannot be viewed only through the lens of the horrific outcome. During a September 5 livestream, Hasan focused on postpartum depression and postpartum psychosis, suggesting that gaps in medical care may have played an important role in what happened.HasanAbi says Lindsay Clancy was “failed by the medical system”HasanAbi's comments centered on the difficulty many people have in understanding severe postpartum mental health conditions. He argued that the public reaction to the case can overlook how drastically postpartum psychosis may affect a person's perception and behavior.The streamer connected that lack of understanding to wider problems within the American healthcare system. He also challenged the idea that an act this disturbing must automatically be explained through ordinary motives such as cruelty.'I kinda understand why people would fail to comprehend what it's like to, you know, have postpartum depression, postpartum psychosis. I feel like these are... this is an unfortunate byproduct of our medical system. Being somewhat patriarchal. Not somewhat, but just, like, it's a byproduct of the existence of a patriarchal system, where the average person looks at such a heinous crime and doesn't understand it. They're like, 'This is not human. It's the most anti-human thing of all time.' A mother killing their own children.”Hasan then made his position on the case more direct. He said he believed there were signs that the system had failed Clancy, while rejecting an alternative theory that her husband had orchestrated the deaths and attempted to frame her.“So, there are numerous instances where the system failed. It's very clear. But I'm not of the mindset that the husband set this up and murdered his children, and then tried to kill Lindsay Clancy, but then failed to do so. Or rather thought that even if she didn't die, that he would be able to pin the blame on her, and then, you know, live the rest of his life. I think that Lindsay Clancy was failed by the medical system; although she did get treatment, it clearly didn't work.”HasanAbi highlights postpartum psychosis evidence in Lindsay Clancy trialHasan also drew attention to the defense's argument about Clancy's mental state. Rather than claiming that postpartum psychosis alone answered every question surrounding the case, he said the evidence presented by the defense deserved consideration when examining her actions.“The question is whether or not she did it. The question is more so whether she did it deliberately or did it as a consequence of postpartum psychosis. And I think that the defense had a decent amount of evidence to show that postpartum psychosis probably played a role in this because I also can't understand why anyone would assume that she just, to take the side of prosecutors, basically, assume that she just did this for the sake of cruelty.”The remarks add another layer to a trial that has drawn intense public attention. HasanAbi's comments do not change the legal questions before the court, but they highlight the broader debate over postpartum mental illness, medical treatment and how responsibility should be understood in cases involving severe psychiatric symptoms.His discussion also shows why the Lindsay Clancy trial continues to generate debate far beyond the courtroom. articles.title: Jake and Callum Robinson: Trial over alleged murders of Australian surfer brothers starts in Mexico
articles.summary: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend were found with gunshot wounds to their heads.
articles.body:
Three men have gone on trial in Mexico for the alleged murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend in 2024.

The bodies of Callum Robinson, his younger brother Jake, and their friend Carter Rhoad from California - all in their early 30s - were found at the bottom of a well with gunshot wounds to their heads, days after they went missing during a surf trip in Baja California.

Prosecutors are seeking jail sentences of more than 200 years for the defendants, who also face charges of violent robbery and auto theft.

The parents of the brothers were in court on Tuesday in the coastal town of Ensenada, telling the media that it was "incredibly important and overwhelmingly difficult".

"We want the men accused of murdering our sons to see, in person, the human consequences of what happened," Martin and Debra Robinson said in a statement, according to Australia's national broadcaster, the ABC.

"Callum and Jake were not simply victims in a case file - they were our sons, deeply loved by their family and friends, with lives, dreams and futures that were brutally taken away."

On the opening day, the accused - Jesús "El Kekas" Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús - were moved to a smaller courtroom amid accusations that some witnesses had been intimidated by people associated with the defendants.

Dozens of witnesses are expected to give evidence during the four-week, judge-only trial.

The 2024 alleged killings of the Robinson brothers and their US friend shocked Australians as well as many residents of the normally peaceful town of Ensenada.

Despite high levels of cartel violence in the northern Mexican border states, tourists are rarely targeted for such violent attacks in Baja California's surf towns.

The ex-girlfriend of one of the accused, Ari Gisell, became the first person to be convicted over the tourists' killings last year and was sentenced to 20 years in prison for her role in their murders.

Mexican prosecutors are pursuing jail sentences of more than 200 years for each of the defendants, as well as an additional 168-year sentence for the alleged ringleader.

Prosecutors say the victims were killed due to a bungled robbery, while the defence argued there was not enough evidence to prove that theory.

Callum Robinson was a member of Australia's national lacrosse team and lived in San Diego where he was a professional lacrosse player.

His younger brother Jake had travelled from Australia for the surf trip and was due to start a job as a doctor when he returned while their friend Rhoad was killed a few months before his wedding.

articles.title: Flight recorders recovered from Amazon cargo jet that overran Miami airport runway, killing five
articles.summary: US News: Investigators have recovered the flight and voice recorders from an Amazon cargo plane that overran the runway at Miami International Airport, killing.
articles.body: Investigators have recovered the flight and voice recorders from an Amazon cargo plane that overran the runway at Miami International Airport, killing five people, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said Monday (local time).All five victims were in a van and an SUV that were among several vehicles struck by the jet outside airport property. The van was carrying seven people from a cleaning company.Homendy called the scene of Sunday’s crash “utter devastation.""It's (debris) pretty extensive. I’m sure it must have been very difficult for the responders as well. I would describe it in one word as devastating, utter devastation,” Homendy said.The van, owned by airline cleaning contractor Professional Ocean Service Corp., was “torn apart,” she added.The NTSB will issue further information Tuesday (local time), potentially including the aircraft’s speed as confirmed by the flight data recorder.The incident also left three people critically injured and two others hospitalised with severe injuries.Federal investigators examining cause of deadly overrunInvestigators are examining whether the plane touched down too late to stop safely.Video of the cargo jet's Sunday landing appears to show the Boeing 767 remaining airborne well down the runway before touching down. Investigators will seek to determine exactly where it landed, whether that was beyond the normal touchdown zone and why the pilots did not abort the landing.They will also examine the plane’s speed and braking, weather and wind conditions, mechanical condition and other factors that may have contributed to the crash.The aircraft flew from Cincinnati to Miami and then to San Juan, Puerto Rico, before returning to Miami. It overran the runway around 2 pm, crossing a road used by warehouse workers and other businesses surrounding the airport.The crash sent thick black smoke into the sky and trapped the pilot and copilot in the cockpit, while some people were trapped in vehicles. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews also had to free a person trapped beneath a vehicle.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: 2 more bodies found, toll climbs to 7; owner earned Rs 4L/month
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police Monday arrested Hariram Gupta (81), who was operating the five-storey PG accommodation that collapsed in south Delhi's Satya N.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police Monday arrested Hariram Gupta (81), who was operating the five-storey PG accommodation that collapsed in south Delhi's Satya Niketan on Sunday, from Bhiwadi in Rajasthan. He is a retired IAF sergeant. Gupta's wife Urmila (75) and their son Mahesh (52) have also been arrested.The toll in Sunday's incident rose to seven after two more bodies were extricated from the rubble early Monday. The deceased students have been identified as Arpit Jaj (19), Abhishek (20), Yuvraj Soni (20), Pawan (17) and Akshat Singh Yadav (18). Two labourers - Surinder Singh (56) and Param Lal Kori (30) - also died in the incident. The rescue and search operation has concluded while a small part of the debris is yet to be cleared.MCD has suspended five south zone officials - deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar, superintending engineer Ranvir Singh, executive engineer (building) Lalit Kumar Goel, assistant engineer (building) Sunil Chauhan and junior engineer (building) Ashish Kumar.In a post on X, CM Rekha Gupta said: "The building owner has been arrested. Immediate sealing of buildings with unauthorised fifth floors has been ordered across Delhi. Nearby PGs and buildings are also being thoroughly inspected. Strict action, including sealing, will be taken against violations. Delhi govt has taken the matter with utmost seriousness. Anyone found guilty or responsible will not be spared." A formal order to seal buildings has, however, not been passed by MCD so far.The probe revealed that construction work had been under way at the property for the past two weeks. Sources said the work included plans to merge two shops, besides carrying out work to address waterlogging. The PG had only one entry and exit point. Investigators have also learned that multiple PG accommodations were being operated in the area under the same name, and are verifying whether they were connected to the same operator."The building was around 40-50 years old and additional floors were added from time to time. There was also commercial space on the premises. The current PG had been operating there for around a year," sources said. Searches are being conducted to trace the PG warden/manager and the labour contractor associated with the building. Their roles in the incident are also being examined.PG netted owner Rs 4L/month Delhi Police, meanwhile, said Hariram was apprehended after raids by over 10 teams were launched to net him. After he was found missing from his Gurgaon home, police used technical surveillance to trace his movements and opened a look-out circular against him to prevent him from leaving the country.A watch was also kept on the premises, including shops, owned by him and his family. The operation was monitored by joint commissioner Nupur Prasad. "Finding himself cornered, Hariram sent some messages seeking help, which alerted us to his location," said a senior cop.Police said five people are being treated for injuries. They have been identified as Asgar Ali (30), Neeraj Bawa (19), Aditya Kumar (19), Nitish Chib (19) and Md Ayan (18). They are undergoing treatment, with two of them reported to be in critical condition.During the investigation, police found the property is registered in the name of Gupta's wife Urmila, but was managed and operated by her husband. Electricity connections for two floors of the building are also registered in his name. Their son, Mahesh, runs a hardware and paint shop.A special team has been formed to investigate the case and officers have sought the ownership documents of the building as well as its map and other permissions.Initial probe and interview with students has revealed around 15 cramped rooms had been carved out in the 55-square-yard house to house 45 students. Three students were lodged in each room and every occupant was charged at least Rs 10,000 per month. The property, sources said, is believed to be generating a revenue of over Rs 4 lakh per month.The probe, sources said, will also extend to "PG mafia" in the area - private players facilitating illegal construction and operation of PGs on commission basis.A purported rent agreement for the PG has also surfaced. It purportedly states: "In case of any personal injury suffered/loss/damage of personal belongings of the tenant due to reasons beyond the control of the PG vize sealing/fire/earthquake/heavy rains/other natural calamities etc, the hostel will not be liable for paying any compensation."The document adds: "PG authorities are not responsible for any casualties to tenants."You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 'Break pattern of impunity': UN experts flag persecution of Pakistan's Ahmadiyya community
articles.summary: Pakistan News: United Nations experts have expressed concerns over reports of human rights violations against members of the Ahmadiyya Muslim community in Pakistan a.
articles.body: United Nations experts have expressed concerns over reports of human rights violations against members of the Ahmadiyya Muslim community in Pakistan and urged authorities to ensure their protection.According to an official release, the experts said, "We are deeply concerned by persistent reports that members of the Ahmadiyya community continue to face harassment, criminal prosecution, violence, and exclusion because of their religious identity.""Every individual has the right to freedom of thought, conscience, religion or belief. No one should be subjected to discrimination, intimidation, or violence, nor should they be prevented from peacefully manifesting their faith or face discrimination with respect to any of their human rights," they added.Experts also highlighted ongoing attacks on Ahmadi places of worship; desecration of graves; interference with peaceful religious observance, including in the context of Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha; arrests and prosecutions related to religious practices or identity; and hate speech."The State has a responsibility to exercise due diligence to prevent human rights violations, investigate allegations promptly and impartially, prosecute those responsible in accordance with international standards, and provide effective remedies to victims," the experts said.“Pakistan must break the pattern of impunity that has allowed perpetrators of attacks and incitement to hatred and violence to act without restraint,” they said. “These attacks take place with tacit official complicity, whilst the cycle of fear prevents people and institutions from upholding the rights and dignity of these minority groups.”They called on the Pakistan government to ensure that all individuals, regardless of their religion or belief, enjoy equal protection under the law without discrimination. The experts also urged the government to review legislation and administrative measures that may be inconsistent with its obligations under international human rights law, including the rights to freedom of religion or belief, freedom of expression, freedom of association and assembly, cultural rights, and equality before the law."Combating religious intolerance requires more than responding to individual incidents," the release cited them as saying. "It requires sustained efforts to foster respect for diversity, counter incitement to hatred and violence, and create an environment in which all religious or belief communities can live in safety and dignity."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Shaibani made his comments during a meeting of Arab foreign ministers at the 166th ministerial session of the Arab League in Cairo, SANA reported. Syria rema...
articles.body:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's commitment to a diplomatic solution with Israel during a meeting of Arab foreign ministers at the Arab League in Cairo.

Shaibani called for exclusive control of arms by the government in order to enhance the country's security, emphasizing it as a sovereign right of the state.

During the meeting, Shaibani condemned Iran's attacks on Gulf Arab states and Jordan, expressing solidarity with the countries that have been targeted.

Shaibani made his comments during a meeting of Arab foreign ministers at the 166th ministerial session of the Arab League in Cairo, SANA reported.

Syria remains committed to a diplomatic solution with Israel, Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Monday, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

"We remain committed to the option of a diplomatic solution and are working hard to achieve it, while working to end Israeli attacks, arrests, and incursions," Shaibani said.

Syrian FM calls for exclusive control of arms

During the meeting, SANA also reported that Shaibani called for the government to have exclusive control of weaponry in order to aid in the country's security.

"Exclusive control of arms is a deterrent decision and an absolute sovereign right of the state, so that we can protect all Syrians and build together," he said.

He also reaffirmed Syria's solidarity with Gulf Arab states and Jordan since the start of the ongoing war against Iran, several of which have come under fire in Iranian attacks . Shaibani condemned Iran's attacks on the Gulf countries during the meeting.
