articles.title: ‘I thought I was dark and I would have to work much harder’: Priyanka Chopra shares a painful fact which impacted her for a long time
articles.summary: Women News: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has often spoken about the hurdles she faced while finding her place in Bollywood. From pay disparity to the unequal treatment o.
articles.body: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has often spoken about the hurdles she faced while finding her place in Bollywood. From pay disparity to the unequal treatment of women on film sets, the actor has been candid about the realities of her early years in the industry. But one experience, she has said, affected how she viewed herself for a long time- being judged for the colour of her skin.In an interview with the BBC’s 100 Women, published on December 6, 2022, Priyanka spoke about the colourism she encountered after entering the film industry.‘I was called black cat, dusky’Recalling her early years in Bollywood, Priyanka said she was called “black cat” and “dusky” because of her complexion. “I thought I was not pretty enough,” she said, explaining how those comments gradually influenced the way she saw herself. She also believed that she would have to work considerably harder to establish herself.What made the experience more complicated, she said, was that she herself felt she could be more talented than some of her lighter-skinned co-stars. Yet she had come to believe that needing to work harder was simply part of the industry.“I believed that I would have to work a lot harder,” Priyanka said, adding that she had assumed it was acceptable because such attitudes were so normalised.Priyanka questioned the idea of ‘dusky’The actor also questioned why complexion had become such an important measure of beauty in India. “I mean, what does ‘dusky’ even mean in a country where we are literally all brown?” she said.For Priyanka, the preference for lighter skin was not simply an issue within the film industry. She connected it to India's colonial history and the lasting social attitudes around fair skin.According to her, the responsibility lies with the present generation to challenge those ideas so that children growing up today do not automatically associate lighter skin with greater beauty or worth.From being judged for her complexion to becoming a global starPriyanka entered the entertainment industry after winning the Miss World title in 2000 and made her acting debut in 2002. She went on to establish herself in Bollywood with films including ‘Andaaz’, ‘Aitraaz’, ‘Krrish’, ‘Don’, ‘Fashion’, ‘7 Khoon Maaf’, ‘Barfi!’ and ‘Mary Kom’.She later made a major transition to Hollywood, becoming the lead of the American television series Quantico. Her international career went on to include films and series such as Baywatch, Isn't It Romantic and The Matrix Resurrections.Priyanka's remarks came at a time when she was also speaking openly about several other inequalities she had experienced during her Bollywood career. Her comments about colourism therefore formed part of a larger reflection on the inequalities she had accepted as normal when she was younger.The journey from being made to question her own appearance to becoming one of India's most recognisable global actors makes her recollection particularly striking. Her comments also underline how deeply colourism can become normalised- not only through what people say to others, but through the way those messages can eventually shape how people see themselves.

articles.title: A 5,000-year-old Polish burial held a necklace made from 42 animal teeth and two human skulls
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Archaeologists in south-western Poland have discovered a burial that appears to date back roughly 5,000 years, containing an adult man, a striking nec.
articles.body: Archaeologists in south-western Poland have discovered a burial that appears to date back roughly 5,000 years, containing an adult man, a striking necklace made from 42 drilled animal teeth and fragments of two human skulls. The grave was found near Żórawina, south of Wrocław, at a site previously known for much later burials. According to Polish Radio, the prehistoric mound was discovered as archaeologists were approaching the end of their summer excavation, revealing evidence of a far older community beneath the soil. Researchers have provisionally dated the burial to shortly before 2900 BCE, although radiocarbon testing is still underway. The unique collection of objects, which also includes amber and bone ornaments, flint tools and a stone battle axe, has raised difficult questions about the identity of the buried man and the meaning of the grave in this part of Europe.5,000-year-old Polish burial preserving a necklace made from 42 animal teethThe discovery came as a surprise to archaeologists working at the Żórawina site. According to Wrocław Medical University, the team had already begun wrapping up its work when they noticed a circular shape in the ground, about 4 metres across, resembling the outline of a burial mound. Excavation of the central chamber revealed a remarkable arrangement of teeth. There were 42 of them, carefully positioned in a pattern that immediately suggested they had once formed a necklace. Each tooth had been drilled through the root, meaning they were deliberately prepared to be threaded onto a cord or string.The material connecting them had disappeared, but their precise arrangement left little doubt about their original purpose. Paweł Dąbrowski, an anthropologist and anatomist at Wrocław Medical University, said the find was clearly a human-made ornament rather than a random collection of animal remains. Researchers believe the teeth came from large mammals. Early observations suggest that they may include teeth from members of the dog family, bears and hoofed animals, while Polish Radio reported that wolves, deer and a young bear are among the possibilities being considered. Scientists have not yet ruled out the presence of human teeth, and DNA testing is expected to provide a clearer answer.The grave revealed an adult man beneath the ancient jewelleryDeeper inside the burial chamber, archaeologists discovered the almost complete skeleton of an adult man, who may have been the original wearer or owner of the extraordinary necklace. The grave also contained bone discs, amber beads, a flint blade or projectile point and a stone battle axe made from serpentinite. The axe has played an important role in the initial dating of the burial. Its shape suggests a date of around 2900 BCE, placing the grave in the Neolithic period and making it thousands of years older than the burials previously excavated at the same location.The wider context makes the discovery particularly significant. The Żórawina site had been known as a cemetery dating mainly to the end of the Roman period and the beginning of the Migration Period, roughly 1,600 years ago. This newly discovered mound therefore pushed the known history of human activity at the site much further into the past. The researchers have suggested that the burial may be connected to communities associated with the ‘Corded Ware cultural circle,’ whose presence and movements across Europe remain important subjects of archaeological research.Why were fragments of two human skulls placed in the graveOne of the most unsettling features of the burial was the presence of remains from two additional human skulls. The fragments were damaged and incomplete, and archaeologists are now investigating why they were placed alongside the buried man. According to Wrocław Medical University, one possibility is that they came from deliberately decapitated individuals and were deposited in the grave as offerings or votive objects. Researchers will closely examine the bones for marks caused by sharp-edged tools, which could either support or challenge that theory. The researchers are treating the discovery cautiously because the condition and incomplete nature of the skull remains make it impossible to determine their story without further analysis.The objects suggest that the buried man may have held an important positionThe combination of a large tooth necklace, weapons and other carefully placed objects has led researchers to wonder whether the man occupied a special position within his community. Dąbrowski has suggested that he may have been a hunter, a warrior or another important figure, while excavation leader Tomasz Gralak proposed that he could have been a patriarch within a family group. The battle axe itself showed signs of use, including slight damage to its blade. This has encouraged the idea that it may have served in combat or hunting rather than simply being a symbolic object. Still, the artefacts cannot provide a definite biography of the man.The Żórawina findings will be compared with similar burial mounds recently discovered at nearby Iwiny. According to both Polish Radio and Wrocław Medical University, bringing together evidence from the two sites could improve understanding of the movements of prehistoric communities in what is now Lower Silesia. Only after the archaeological, genetic and scientific studies are completed may the strange combination of teeth, skulls and weapons begin to reveal the fuller story behind this 5,000-year-old burial.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Indonesia air travel resumes after two-day disruption from volcanic ash
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from Anak .
articles.body: Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau, which disrupted nearly 3,000 flights.Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and Halim Perdanakusuma Airport in Jakarta, along with Husein Sastranegara Airport in West Java’s Bandung and two smaller airports in Banten province, reopened shortly after midnight, Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.Three other airports, including Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung at the southern end of Sumatra, remained closed until 10 a.m. despite improving conditions. Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, South Sumatra, resumed normal operations on Monday morning.“We are taking a cautious approach because wind direction can change rapidly,” Purwagandhi said in a statement. “We want to make sure volcanic ash has moved away from airports around Anak Krakatau.”While tests at several airports found no traces of volcanic ash, the prolonged closures would provide additional time to inspect and clean runways, taxiways, aircraft and other equipment that may have been exposed to the ash, Purwagandhi said.The continuous eruption at Anak Krakatau, marked by lava fountains and loud explosions, subsided on Sunday, but the volcanic island remained active on Tuesday morning. Eruptions were recorded at 5:08 a.m. and 5:34 a.m., although the height of the ash column could not be determined.A massive two-day air travel disruption affected approximately 341,000 passengers as airport closures on Sunday and Monday grounded nearly 2,961 flights—including 622 international routes—according to reports by the Associated Press.The government also allowed schools in areas affected by volcanic ash to temporarily switch to online classes to limit students’ exposure to the ash.Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait, located between Indonesia’s main islands of Java and Sumatra. Its name means “child of Krakatau” and refers to the volcano that emerged from the remnants of the infamous Krakatau, whose massive 1883 eruption triggered a period of global cooling.In 2018, an eruption of Anak Krakatau generated a tsunami that killed at least 430 people across Sumatra and Java. Researchers believe the volcanic activity triggered an underwater landslide, causing part of the volcano’s southwestern slope to collapse and displace a large volume of seawater.The volcano has remained at Indonesia’s second-highest alert level since July, with authorities urging residents, tourists and fishermen to stay at least 3 kilometres (1.9 miles) away from the active crater.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US designates 15-year-old Italian tech collective as terror organisation; forcing it to shut down; Company says: Day we discovered, ⁠we are ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: For 15 years, Autistici/Inventati had operated as a volunteer-run refuge for activists and campaigners seeking alternatives to commercial online platf.
articles.body: For 15 years, Autistici/Inventati had operated as a volunteer-run refuge for activists and campaigners seeking alternatives to commercial online platforms. Then a US terrorism designation forced the Italian technology collective to shut its doors. According to a recent report by the news agency Reuters, the group has now announced that it will end its services after the designation triggered the suspension of its .org domain and the closure of its bank account. The shutdown affects a substantial user base. The closure impacts about 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists and 10,000 blogs, according to figures from the US State Department.​A collective built on privacy-focused digital tools​Founded in 2001, Autistici/Inventati, known as A/I, provided privacy-focused email, websites, mailing lists and blogging services. Its stated purpose was to offer activists, campaigners and others a space outside mainstream commercial platforms, where data practices and content policies are often shaped by corporate interests.​The organisation described itself in different terms than US officials. A/I rejected the terrorism designation, describing itself as a collective of volunteers and digital activists that provides digital self-defence tools for activists, individuals, groups and associations.​Washington's designation set off a chain of consequences​The US designated the group on August 26, alleging it provided support to extremist activists and organisations through services including email accounts, websites and communications tools. The allegation triggered a rapid sequence of institutional responses that A/I said left it unable to continue operating, the Reuters report noted.​Two days after the designation, autistici.org became unreachable after Public Interest Registry (PIR), the US-based operator of the .org domain, placed it on serverHold status. PIR said it was legally required to suspend the domain following the designation, framing its action as compliance rather than an independent judgment on the group's activities.​The financial consequences followed soon after. Banca Etica, an Italian lender where the collective held an account, subsequently suspended the account, citing sanctions-related risks. The bank criticised what it described as the use of US sanctions for political purposes, a characterisation that placed it at odds with the rationale behind Washington's designation.​A group that says it tried to keep operating​In a statement announcing the closure, A/I told Reuters it had hoped to continue operating but could no longer do so responsibly. The collective described its initial response to the designation as one of defiance rather than immediate retreat. "The day we discovered we had been designated a global terrorist organisation, we promised that we would try to resist as long as this was possible," the collective said.​That resistance, however, gave way to concerns about the people connected to the organisation rather than the organisation itself. A/I said it had "a responsibility to protect our users" and could not ignore the risk that people associated with the organisation might face legal or financial consequences.​Weighing the risk to users over continued operation​The collective's explanation centred on the potential fallout for people only loosely connected to its work, rather than on the designation's direct effect on its own infrastructure. "The possibility that our work may cause legal and financial consequences to those who are close to us, or even only have something to do with us, leaves us no choice," it said.​The statement did not detail what legal avenues, if any, remain open to challenge the designation.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: KT Rama Rao, among BRS leaders booked for assaulting cops outside Telangana assembly
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Telangana Police on Tuesday registered an FIR against BRS leaders KT Rama Rao, T Harish Rao, Gangula Kamalakar and others for allegedly obs.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Telangana Police on Tuesday registered an FIR against BRS leaders KT Rama Rao, T Harish Rao, Gangula Kamalakar and others for allegedly obstructing and assaulting police officials outside the Telangana assembly.According to the FIR, the leaders allegedly abused women constables, threatened staff and caught police officials by the collar. The FIR further said that the leaders tried to force entry despite security restrictions imposed on the Assembly Speaker's orders.The case is booked under Sections 121(1), 132, 74, 79, 351, 352, 353 r/w 3(5) of the BNS. Investigation is on.The FIR came after BRS legislators staged a protest against the Congress government, leading to a confrontation between opposition leaders and police personnel. Several BRS leaders, including KT Rama Rao and T Harish Rao, were detained.During the Assembly proceedings, Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar broke down while recounting the alleged remarks and the circumstances surrounding the incident. The episode drew strong reactions from ruling party members, who demanded action against BRS MLC Tata Madhu.Congress condemned the alleged remarks and demanded an apology from Tata Madhu, while BRS rejected the allegations.Tata Madhu denied insulting the Speaker, maintaining that his comments were directed at police personnel in the context of the confrontation during the protest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Strike our assets & you get struck': Iran threatens US energy assets in Gulf after latest clashes
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran has threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, warning that American oil and gas interests and energy infrastructure acros.
articles.body: Iran has threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, warning that American oil and gas interests and energy infrastructure across the Gulf could be targeted as tensions escalate over the Strait of Hormuz."Strike our assets and you get struck," Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said after US and Iranian forces traded strikes on shipping over the weekend, pushing oil prices to near six-week highs on Monday, according to Reuters.The warning came amid growing concerns that the conflict could escalate further, with diplomatic efforts showing little progress towards restoring normal energy flows through the Gulf.Iran tightens restrictionsIran has tightened restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and gas supplies, since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28.On Sunday, senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would soon announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf and establish a new shipping corridor through the strait.Rezaei said the restricted zone would begin where a US naval blockade of Iran starts and extend into parts of the Gulf. Ships entering the area would be placed on an Iranian sanctions list."We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran," Rezaei said.Qalibaf later reinforced the warning in an apparent response to US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had described Iran's oil tanker fleet as "defenceless"."It's simple: the oil and gas production chain here is sprawling, accessible, and exposed. American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, wrote on X.Oil flows disruptedTensions have intensified after a relative lull through much of August and the collapse of an interim ceasefire reached in June.Earlier on Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The strikes followed attacks by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region.Shipping data showed that an average of only 10 commodity vessels a day passed through the Strait of Hormuz over the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. The strait is a critical energy chokepoint. Before the war, it carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.Regional tensions were also heightened by Israeli strikes on a town in southern Lebanon that killed at least 12 people on Monday, according to Lebanon's health ministry.The strikes have raised fears of a renewed Israeli military campaign despite a June ceasefire with Iran-backed Hezbollah. Tehran has insisted that any lasting agreement with Washington must include an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon.Iran has said it will step up efforts to address problems caused by US sanctions, which have put further pressure on its economy.Three senior Iranian sources told Reuters that Washington's campaign to restrict Iranian oil exports and curb sanctions evasion is becoming increasingly difficult for Tehran to withstand.Qalibaf acknowledged over the weekend that Iran's challenges extend beyond the battlefield. Alongside the military conflict, he cited inflation, unemployment, currency volatility and market instability as major domestic problems.The conflict has also affected Gulf oil producers, including the United Arab Emirates, which has faced Iranian missile attacks and attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.The disruption is also being felt in the United States, where higher fuel prices have added to economic pressures and could weigh on President Donald Trump's popularity ahead of November's midterm elections.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
